title: Amplified basses and the hunt for a full-size bass
summary: Breaux dislikes electric amplifiers and Fender basses and wants a true tone. They discuss what became of a late bassist's full-size bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You play it more easier? Yeah, but you don't get the
true tone. You know what I mean?
You said you don't like the electric amplifier on the bass then? No, I don't.
What about these Fender basses? I don't like them either. I mean, I just like the old-time, old-style bass. They give you a true
tone. Bro, you don't know anyone that has a full-size bass, huh?

No, the last one I had a full-size bass. I don't know what happened to it. The old man that died Alba Grunin? Yeah. They tell me his wife had it, but when I went to see her, it was gone. I don't know if
They saw that this woman on St. Peter Street, she saw that something down north.
I didn't see it, but I understand it was a full-size bass.

Well, if other boys have been worrying about a full-size bass, if I could get in touch with one. You never found out about Eddie Jackson's bass, huh? Oh, no, I didn't hear. Andrew Morgan was letting know about it, but I never did. Eddie Jackson had tuba. He had tuba, but he didn't play bass too.
